Fit latent class models with different numbers of classes, and compare them

Source: R/lpa.R
enumerate_lca.Rd

enumerate_lca() fits latent class models with different numbers of classes to examine heterogeneity in categorical response patterns. It brings together evidence about fit, classification, and estimation stability to support selection of the number of classes. Each fitted candidate remains available for examination of its class-specific response probabilities and class proportions.

Usage

enumerate_lca(data, vars, n_classes = 1:4, ...)

Arguments

data

A data frame with one row per observation.

vars

Names of the categorical indicator columns.

n_classes

Numbers of classes to compare, specified as positive integers. Default 1:4.

...

Further arguments for multilca(), used for every candidate, such as missing ("error" or "fiml"), n_starts, seed and min_probability. id and n_group_classes are not accepted, and neither is model: a latent class model has no covariance structure. Every indicator is categorical unless named in ordinal or count. categorical is accepted but has no further effect; its names must be in vars.

Value

An object of class multilpa_enumeration, as enumerate_classes() returns. get_candidates() (also as.data.frame()) gives one row per candidate with its log likelihood, information criteria, entropy, convergence and replication; get_best() and summary() the candidate with the lowest value of each criterion; plot() the criteria against the number of classes; and get_candidate() one fitted candidate. The number of classes is in the n_profiles column of the candidates table, and get_candidate() selects it through its n_profiles argument. A candidate that could not be fitted keeps its row, with NA values.

Details

This is the single-level interface to enumerate_classes() for categorical indicators. Every indicator is categorical unless named in ordinal or count, as in lca().

For observations nested in groups, use enumerate_classes() with the grouping column as id and the indicators as categorical.

Conditions

latents_bad_argument when id or n_group_classes is passed, or when model is passed (no indicator is continuous); latents_bad_categorical when categorical names a column not in vars. A candidate with more free parameters than the table of response patterns has free cells warns with class latents_unidentified. A latents_single_start message names the candidates whose best log likelihood was reached from one start only.

See also

lca() to fit one model; enumerate_lpa() for continuous indicators.

Examples

models <- enumerate_lca(student_esm, c("time_with_friends",
                                       "on_social_media", "tv_video_games",
                                       "sports"),
                        n_classes = 1:3, n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
#> 1 of 3 candidates reached their best log likelihood from one start only (classes3); refit those you consider with more starts.
summary(models)
#> Class enumeration: 3 candidates, 3 converged, 0 failed to fit
#> 3 distinct candidate(s) are minimal under some criterion.
